population: Non-constipating IBS (IBS-D, IBS-M); no biomarker selection
note: Gut-restricted TPH inhibitors (LX1031, LX1033) lowered patient urinary/plasma 5-HIAA exactly as mouse gut-5-HT data predicted, but no IBS disease model ever existed: LX1031 gave week-1 relief in 155 patients (2011), LX1033 then missed stool consistency in 373 (2013, unpublished) and Lexicon moved the class to carcinoid syndrome.
label: IBS (TPH1 inhibitors)

engagement.note: Class proxies LP-533401/LP-615819 cut mouse gut 5-HT dose-dependently and spared brain 5-HT; ferret cisplatin emesis was the only functional readout.
engagement.quote: Similar to the Tph1 knockout results, these TPH inhibitors have the ability to selectively reduce 5-HT levels in the murine GI tract without affecting brain 5-HT levels.
engagement.judgement: Abstract-level only (JPET 2008 is not in PMC). Liu 2008 characterises LP-533401/LP-615819, class proxies; LX1031 itself (the 3'-methoxy analog) was dosed in mice only in Lexicon abstracts summarised by Camilleri 2011 (NGM, review).

engagement.note: Urinary 5-HIAA fell 25% (median) at 1000 mg QID and tracked relief; paper says preclinical, phase 1 and phase 2 agree.
engagement.quote: LX1031 has been shown consistently to reduce mucosal 5-HT production in preclinical models, in a phase 1 study of normal volunteers, and now in a phase 2 study of nonconstipating IBS patients.
engagement.judgement: Full text read (PMC4905727). NCT00813098, n=155, biomarker substudy n=76; results first posted 2010-12-02. The sentence puts preclinical models, healthy volunteers and patients side by side but gives no quantitative scaling (mouse jejunal 5-HT fell 33-66%; patient urinary 5-HIAA fell 25%), so magnitude = direction_only. Not 'neg': LX1033 (NCT01494233, n=373) also lowered plasma 5-HIAA while missing efficacy (Lexicon FY2013 10-K / Feb-2014 8-K) but that is a sponsor filing, not a paper, registry result or FDA document, so it carries no status.

dose.note: Mouse jejunal 5-HT fell 33–66% at 15–135 mg/kg/day; patients needed 4 g/day for a 25% 5-HIAA fall; never compared.
dose.short: Mouse %5-HT fall never mapped to dose
dose.quote: This class of compounds has unique properties with respect to pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic effects on GI serotonin production.
dose.judgement: The mouse LX1031 numbers (15/45/135 mg/kg/day -> ~33/51/66% jejunal 5-HT reduction) are quoted from Camilleri 2011 (NGM review, PMC3076306) citing Lexicon abstracts; the patient number (25% median urinary 5-HIAA fall at 1000 mg QID, plasma flat above 750 mg QID) is from Brown 2011. No primary source maps one onto the other, and Camilleri 2011 states no dose-response using colonic transit or sensation was ever reported. Brown 2011 itself says non-responders 'might' respond at higher doses, i.e. the dose target was unresolved.

efficacy.model: Tph1-knockout mouse biochemistry + ferret emesis (no IBS model)
efficacy.note: No IBS disease model: the case rested on Tph1-knockout biochemistry, ferret cisplatin emesis and the 5-HT3-antagonist clinical precedent.
efficacy.short: No IBS model; ferret emesis only
efficacy.quote: These findings suggest that GI-specific TPH inhibitors may provide novel treatments for various gastrointestinal disorders associated with dysregulation of the GI serotonergic system, such as chemotherapy-induced emesis and irritable bowel syndrome.
efficacy.judgement: Deliberately not 'same' on Brown 2011: that paper tests a mechanistic hypothesis (less mucosal 5-HT -> fewer symptoms) against patients, but no preclinical model ever made an IBS efficacy prediction (no visceral hypersensitivity, secretion or diarrhoea model was run), so there is no model prediction to score. Brown 2011's primary endpoint separated only at week 1 (47.5% vs 22.0%, P=.018); stool consistency was a secondary endpoint.

efficacy.model: Mouse GI transit / colonic motility (LX1033, telotristat dosed)
efficacy.note: LX1033 and telotristat left mouse transit, gastric emptying and colonic motility unchanged; paper credits IBS benefit to anti-inflammation, no patient comparison.
efficacy.quote: Peripheral TPH inhibitors, therefore, fail to alter constitutive gastrointestinal motility significantly, despite their ability to reduce mucosal levels of 5-HT profoundly.
efficacy.judgement: Second untested entry added because this is the first functional (motility) model run with the actual IBS drug (LX1033), published while NCT01494233 (primary endpoint stool consistency) was enrolling. Full text read (PMC4034681): the authors mention the 'utility' of TPH inhibitors in non-constipating IBS next to the flat mouse motility and attribute it to the anti-inflammatory effect in TNBS colitis, which is not a prediction-vs-outcome comparison, hence comparison_stated=false and no 'contra'. The LX1033 trial then showed no stool-consistency separation from placebo (sponsor 10-K FY2013; no registry results, no paper), so the mouse 'no motility effect' was never formally scored against patients.

safety.note: Brain 5-HT spared in mice predicts no pCPA-like affective effects; 4-week trials saw no CNS signal, but no comparison was published.
safety.quote: Mice lacking Tph1 contain little to no 5-HT in the blood and GI tract while maintaining normal levels in the brain.
safety.judgement: Brown 2011 reports AEs evenly distributed, no ECG/lab abnormalities, and attributes the 'favorable safety profile' to local action and low systemic exposure, but never names the rodent brain-5-HT prediction; only Camilleri 2011 (review) sets the two side by side ('lack of effect on brain 5-HT in several species suggest that LX-1031 is unlikely to cause affective disorders'). A lenient scorer could call Brown 2011 'same'. The Tph1-knockout cardiac phenotype (Cote 2003) and Camilleri's open questions (constipation, platelets, ischaemic colitis) were never tested beyond 4-week trials.
